newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian bonds lifted by technicals, rumours.
newsitem.headline: Australian bonds lifted by technicals, rumours.

text.p: Australian bond futures ended at their highest level since the Federal Reserve tightened policy in March, supported by technical buying, traders said.

There were also rumours in initial trading that the long awaited "living wage" claim verdict by the Australian Industrials Relations Commission was about to be announced and that it was going to be a moderate outcome, they added.

"The living wage claim rumour certainly encouraged the early move. Physical flows have not matched the activity in futures by any means, and if anything, stock has been offered ahead of tomorrow's tender," one trader said.

The Australian Treasury is offering A$300 million each of the April 2000 and the October 2007 stocks at a tender on Tuesday, although in the market's current bullish mood traders saw no trouble in absorbing the stock.

The early advance took the 10-year bond futures contract out of the bearish downward channel that has been running since late February, fuelled by profit-taking by computerised U.S. hedge funds on short postions.
It also allowed the market to make another strong outperformance against the U.S. and Canada, which both continue to fret over the possibility of further Fed tightenings.
Friday's U.S. labour force report was seen cementing fears that the Fed will tighten policy again when the Federal Open market committee meets in May.
Local jobs data for March are due on Thursday and expected to show only a moderate rise in employment, leaving the unemployment rate above 8.5 percent.

Meanwhile, and despite the early strong rumours, no news emanated from the AIRC on the national "living wage" claim. The commission has said that it would notify all parties before it made a formal statement on its decision.

Yield spreads to the U.S. and Canada were sharply tighter, particularly against the latter which continues to be plagued by a weaking Canadian dollar in the wake of last month's Fed move. New Zealand market took some inspiration from the Australian rally, although it heavily underperformed last week.

The 10-year bond contract broke out of a bearish channel after breaking 91.920, but ran into resistance at the 92.000 psychological level. A break of 92.020, the high seen briefly in SYCOM on March 25, confirms the bullish tone, analysts added.
